It's no doubt Cyberpunk 2077 will go down as one of the most broken and botched releases of a video game ever. That being said, over two years after the game's release they've finally managed to fix most of the game-breaking bugs (my game still completely crashed every 10-12 hours of gameplay though - your mileage may vary).

The gameplay mechanics and loot-n'-shoot combat are the best I've experienced since Borderlands 2, cyberware is awesome, the story is solid, the soundtrack has a ton of bangers, and the characters aren't bad either. The real thing that engrossed me, though, was Night City. It just oozes personality, although thanks to current events it's starting to feel less and less like a far-future dystopian nightmare. If you have a mid range PC from the past 3 years, give it a try. Anything older than that... good luck.

I bought the Cyberpunk 2020 game book in 1994. I have wanted to visit Night City ever since. The world of R. Talisorian's Cyberpunk, and cyberpunk fiction in general, has been a huge inspiration for my music, my creativity, everything - as all those who know me are well aware.

I am happy to report that the gritty nature of its roots has not been lost in translation for new audiences. This world is not a shinier and happier version of 2020. It's exactly what we envisioned while netrunning back in the day, just with the updates one could expect from 57 years of in-story advancement.

I can now run the streets of Night City in what might be a new entry in my top-5 favorite games, giving me a feeling that I haven't had since Deus Ex: HR and the newest returns to the world of Shadowrun.

I feel like I'm home.

This was well worth the wait.

Not a perfect game, but by far some of the most fun I have had in an RPG. The game is filled with quests that add so much flavour to a world that has lost it's soul to corporations and the lust for power, and game play designed to give you so many different ways to approach an objective. The characters are fun, flawed and so deeply human, and just like most modern open world RPGs, the story takes a backseat to the truly massive open world for you to explore and lose yourself in, and peel back the flashy, beautiful veneer that hides a malicious and disgusting world obsessed with power and status.

The game is awesome but I cannot help but be frustrated with the steam deck version.

Being marked as "verified" is misleading as I have not had any game cause me more issues on my steam deck than Cyberpunk 2077 ; audio issues, performance issues, crashes, problems with the launcher...

A little tweaking around could probably lift up a fair amount of annoyances but that is not what a "verified" experience is about in my opinion.

Its a hard game to run and crazy that it is possible to do so on steam deck but straight up pretending it is a flawless out of the box experience for the deck is false information.

Lets just say you hypothetically do 5 playthroughs of cyberpunk ultimate edition on xbox and you crack Panam every time. Now lets say hypothetically you get cyberpunk on steam family to crack Panam with ray tracing and do your 6th playthrough. Now hypothetically you realize you cant post a review until you actually buy the game.

Lets just say im hypothetically..
Perhaps if I had played it when it was first released, my review would be different, but if you play it now, I am sure you won't regret it.

This game also has Judy Alvarez. She is the best character ever. I love Judy.

Based on the game as presented, with the good (gameplay, story, etc) and the bad (buggy launch, cut features, etc), I give this game a 8/10.

Based on the fact that this game has Judy Alvarez in it...

The atmosphere in Cyberpunk 2077 is like if you were to grab the best elements from several different sci-fi/cyberpunk movies and games in the past, but make it trashy. Give all the girls chola tattoos, and put dildo sex shops around every corner.

The game has no color palette, and every neon color imaginable is vomited onto the screen in an ocean of bipolarity. It's not hot or cool, it's just every color imaginable blasted to the max. Like a never ending rave.

The gunplay is seriously just OK, and the driving is fucking atrocious. Seriously, the driving is ATROCIOUS. The amount of mods needed to make this game more palatable is silly.

Story is ok, a little silly. The lore isn't that deep, but mildly interesting. The bit about MS still being uncured was interesting. Deus Ex is an objectively superior cyberpunk game in almost every way. If you need dildos and porn in your video game to hold your attention, then I guess this is it dawg.

If you have no problem with playing an unfinished game, go ahead. Otherwise wait a year or two and play witcher instead.

New review:

With the release of 1.0, weirdly enough named 1.5 by the devs, the game is finally in a recommendable state. It's still not what I hoped it would be, the 40 minute gameplay demo they released before launch is a straight up other game, but I would be lying if I said it isn't a good game. It's very much in the vain of the witcher 3 where the narrative, both in main and side quests, is excellent but anything outside of that is just passable. It never reaches witcher 3 heights but it gets damn close.

I've spent many hours now replaying the game, mostly because of the mods but also that it's just a comfortable gaming experience. Like grinding a new COD game. Doesn't need a lot of thinking, just sit back and relax. For sure not a good thing, but not a bad thing either.

7/10

There are two games to date that I have had sit through the end credits to process what I just played.
That being Red Dead Redemption 2, and this.

This game is truly an experience.

Cyberpunk is that gem you thought it's average but it turned out to be diamond 

Truly blown away by story telling, music, RPG mechanics and Night City world. V as Character is very well written and performed by female actor and the game has got a lot of replayability as well however, there is no NG+ which is lame! There should be as it will encourage players to give one more playthrough without having to regrind all skills weapons again.

Night City 
The world design is meticulously designed of course that came with almost a decade worth of time of development, however Night City still feels empty due to there is no intereaction with our protagonist (V) there are no random side events, no NPC is talking to you but I think that was the message CDPR wanted to deliver that even as lively world and so many people around you, you could still be lonely. 

DLC Phantom Liberty 
Now that's how you make a DLC no doubt there. CDPR is known for their top tier DLC experience witnessing Songbird's story arc was quiet good experience actually, a must buy DLC.

Performance 
Runs pretty well after so many patches just had 2 crashes in my entire playthrough.

Highly Recommended 8/10
